```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5,
  fig.align = "center"
)
library(distmer)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
bray <- vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
```

An overall model can show that community composition differs among groups, but
it does not say which ecological comparisons are responsible. This guide uses
the four management classes in `vegan::dune` to move from one overall question
to planned contrasts, all pairwise comparisons, and multiplicity control.

```{r overview}
management <- data.frame(Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management))
m1 <- permanova(bray ~ Management, management, permutations = 499, seed = 41)
summary(m1)
```

The ordination is a visual summary, not the test itself. The model uses the
complete Bray--Curtis matrix, whereas the plot shows only two axes.

```{r ordination, fig.alt="Dune sites in a two-axis PCoA coloured by management class"}
ord <- cmdscale(bray, k = 2)
ord_plot <- data.frame(
  Axis1 = ord[, 1], Axis2 = ord[, 2], Management = management$Management
)

ggplot() +
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_point(data = ord_plot, aes(Axis1, Axis2, fill = Management), shape=21, size = 3) +
  stat_ellipse(data = ord_plot, aes(Axis1, Axis2, colour = Management), linewidth = 0.6, type = "norm",
               show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Dune communities by management",
       x = "PCoA axis 1", y = "PCoA axis 2", colour = "Management")
```

## Start with ecological questions

A planned contrast is most useful when it expresses a question chosen before
looking at the pairwise results. Here we compare biological farming with hobby
farming, and the average of the two more intensively managed classes with the
average of the other two classes. Coefficients are applied to equally weighted
group centroids and must sum to zero.

```{r design}
design <- compile_permanova_design(~ Management, management, bray)
planned <- rbind(
  `biological - hobby farming` = c(BF = 1, HF = -1, NM = 0, SF = 0),
  `BF/HF mean - NM/SF mean` = c(BF = 0.5, HF = 0.5, NM = -0.5, SF = -0.5)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_contrasts(
  design, planned, adjust = "holm", permutations = 499, seed = 41
)
planned_fit$table
```

Each contrast keeps the remaining group structure in the model, then obtains a
permutation p-value for that comparison. Holm adjustment protects the family
of planned questions without assuming that the contrasts are independent.

## All pairwise comparisons

When there is no small set of pre-specified comparisons,
`permanova_pairwise()` constructs every pair. The raw p-value describes one
comparison; the adjusted value accounts for having examined the complete
family.

```{r pairwise}
pw <- permanova_pairwise(
  design, adjust = "holm", permutations = 499, seed = 41
)
pw$table[, c("contrast", "pseudo_f", "p_perm", "p_adjusted")]
```

```{r pairwise-plot, fig.alt="Adjusted p-values for all pairwise management comparisons"}
pw_plot <- pw$table
pw_plot$contrast <- reorder(pw_plot$contrast, pw_plot$p_adjusted)

ggplot(pw_plot, aes(p_adjusted, contrast)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = p_adjusted, yend = contrast),
               colour = "grey75") +
  geom_point(size = 2.7, colour = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Pairwise management comparisons",
       x = "Holm-adjusted permutation p-value", y = NULL)
```

Do not interpret a non-significant pair as proof that its communities are
equivalent. It says only that this analysis did not resolve a difference at the
chosen error rate and permutation depth.

## Comparisons adjusted for other predictors

In a multifactor model, a management contrast needs an explicit rule for
averaging over other categorical predictors. `weights = "equal"` describes an
equally represented ecological population; `weights = "proportional"`
describes the observed sample composition.

```{r marginal}
factors <- data.frame(
  Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management),
  Use = droplevels(dune.env$Use)
)
multifactor <- compile_permanova_design(~ Management + Use, factors, bray)

permanova_marginal_contrasts(
  multifactor, factor = "Management", contrasts = planned,
  weights = "equal", permutations = 199, seed = 41
)$table
```

If a factor interacts with a numeric environmental gradient, its comparison
also depends on where that gradient is evaluated. The reference value is
therefore supplied rather than silently chosen.

```{r adjusted}
env <- data.frame(
  Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management),
  Use = droplevels(dune.env$Use),
  A1 = dune.env$A1
)
adjusted_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management * A1 + Use, env, bray
)

permanova_adjusted_contrasts(
  adjusted_design, factor = "Management", contrasts = planned,
  at = c(A1 = mean(env$A1)), weights = "equal",
  permutations = 199, seed = 41
)$table
```

## Choosing familywise protection

For most ecological reports, Holm-adjusted planned or pairwise comparisons are
a clear default. `distmer` also provides two shared-permutation procedures:

- `permanova_maxT_pairwise()` compares every statistic with the largest value
  in each common-null permutation. Its familywise guarantee is for the
  complete null in which all group centroids coincide.
- `permanova_pairwise_strong()` uses closed testing and protects every pair
  even when other pairs genuinely differ.

```{r simultaneous}
max_f <- permanova_maxT_pairwise(design, permutations = 199, seed = 41)
closed <- permanova_pairwise_strong(design, permutations = 199, seed = 41)

max_f$table[, c("contrast", "p_perm", "p_maxT")]
closed$table[, c("contrast", "p_perm", "p_closed")]
```

The strong finite-sample guarantee has an important boundary. It applies to
pairwise equality of **complete distributions** for independent one-factor
observations. It is not a strong guarantee for centroid-only nulls when groups
have different dispersion or shape. Use the distance and dispersion checks in
`vignette("dispersion")` alongside these comparisons.

## What to report

Report the contrast coefficients or pair labels, their ecological rationale,
the raw and adjusted p-values, the adjustment method, the dissimilarity, the
number of permutations, and the seed. A pseudo-F is an effect-to-residual ratio,
not an effect size; show an ordination or centroid-distance summary as well.
